1	import Foundation
2	
3	struct ThreadCardRowProjector {
4	    let hosts: [DockHostConfiguration]
5	    let hostIdentityResolver: DockHostIdentityResolver
6	    let localMetadata: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
7	    let now: @Sendable () -> Date
8	
9	    func rows(from cards: [DockThreadCardDTO], sourceHostID: String? = nil) -> [DockRowViewModel] {
10	        cards.filter(\.isAppFacingHumanThreadCard).map { card in
11	            makeRow(card: card, sourceHostID: sourceHostID)
12	        }
13	    }
14	
15	    func cachedPinnedRows(excluding loadedKeys: Set<LocalThreadMetadataKey>) -> [DockRowViewModel] {
16	        return localMetadata.compactMap { key, metadata in
17	            guard metadata.isPinned,
18	                  metadata.hasAppFacingHumanPinnedDisplay,
19	                  !loadedKeys.contains(key),
20	                  hostIdentityResolver.logicalHostID(forAlias: key.hostID) != nil else {
21	                return nil
22	            }
23	            return cachedPinnedRow(key: key, metadata: metadata)
24	        }
25	    }
26	
27	    func makeRow(card: DockThreadCardDTO, sourceHostID: String? = nil) -> DockRowViewModel {
28	        let id = HostScopedThreadID(hostID: card.logicalHostID, threadID: card.threadID)
29	        let metadata = metadata(
30	            for: id,
31	            backendSessionID: card.backendSessionID,
32	            sourceHostID: sourceHostID
33	        )
34	        let activityDate = activityDate(for: card)
35	        return DockRowViewModel(
36	            id: id,
37	            sourceHostID: sourceHostID,
38	            backendSessionID: card.backendSessionID,
39	            title: nonEmpty(card.title) ?? "Thread \(shortThreadID(card.threadID))",
40	            hostDisplayName: nonEmpty(card.hostDisplayName)
41	                ?? hostDisplayName(for: card.logicalHostID, sourceHostID: sourceHostID),
42	            hostEndpoint: nonEmpty(card.hostEndpoint)
43	                ?? hostEndpoint(for: card.logicalHostID, sourceHostID: sourceHostID),
44	            repository: nonEmpty(card.repository) ?? nonEmpty(card.workingDirectory) ?? "Unknown workspace",
45	            branch: nonEmpty(card.branch) ?? "No branch",
46	            status: status(for: card.status),
47	            lastActivity: relativeTime(since: activityDate),
48	            lastActivityDate: activityDate,
49	            orderKey: card.orderKey,
50	            summary: nonEmpty(card.displaySummary) ?? "No summary",
51	            rail: metadata?.rail ?? rail(for: card),
52	            label: metadata?.label,
53	            origin: origin(for: card),
54	            relationship: relationship(for: card),
55	            isPinned: metadata?.isPinned ?? false,
56	            pinnedAt: metadata?.pinnedAt,
57	            pinnedOrder: metadata?.pinnedOrder
58	        )
59	    }
60	
61	    private func cachedPinnedRow(
62	        key: LocalThreadMetadataKey,
63	        metadata: LocalThreadMetadata
64	    ) -> DockRowViewModel {
65	        let snapshot = metadata.lastKnownPinnedDisplay
66	        let fallbackDate = metadata.pinnedAt ?? Date.distantPast
67	        let resolved = hostIdentityResolver.resolve(rowHostID: key.hostID)
68	        let logicalHostID = resolved?.logicalHostID ?? key.hostID
69	        return DockRowViewModel(
70	            id: HostScopedThreadID(hostID: logicalHostID, threadID: key.threadID),
71	            sourceHostID: resolved?.host.id,
72	            backendSessionID: key.backendSessionID,
73	            title: nonEmpty(snapshot?.title) ?? "Not loaded",
74	            hostDisplayName: hostDisplayNameForCachedRow(hostID: key.hostID, snapshot: snapshot),
75	            hostEndpoint: hostEndpointForCachedRow(hostID: key.hostID, snapshot: snapshot),
76	            repository: nonEmpty(snapshot?.repository) ?? "Unknown workspace",
77	            branch: nonEmpty(snapshot?.branch) ?? "No branch",
78	            status: snapshot?.status ?? .dormant,
79	            lastActivity: nonEmpty(snapshot?.lastActivity) ?? "Not loaded",
80	            lastActivityDate: snapshot?.lastActivityDate ?? fallbackDate,
81	            summary: nonEmpty(snapshot?.summary) ?? "This pinned thread is not loaded yet.",
82	            rail: metadata.rail ?? snapshot?.rail ?? .blue,
83	            label: metadata.label ?? snapshot?.label,
84	            origin: snapshot?.originKind.sessionOrigin ?? .unknown(),
85	            relationship: snapshot?.relationship ?? .root,
86	            isPinned: true,
87	            pinnedAt: metadata.pinnedAt,
88	            pinnedOrder: metadata.pinnedOrder
89	        )
90	    }
91	
92	    private func metadata(
93	        for id: HostScopedThreadID,
94	        backendSessionID: String,
95	        sourceHostID: String?
96	    ) -> LocalThreadMetadata? {
97	        let exactKey = LocalThreadMetadataKey(
98	            hostID: id.hostID,
99	            backendSessionID: backendSessionID,
100	            threadID: id.threadID
101	        )
102	        if let metadata = localMetadata[exactKey] {
103	            return metadata
104	        }
105	
106	        return localMetadata.first { key, _ in
107	            guard key.backendSessionID == backendSessionID,
108	                  key.threadID == id.threadID else {
109	                return false
110	            }
111	            return hostIdentityResolver.logicalHostID(
112	                forAlias: key.hostID,
113	                sourceConfiguredHostID: sourceHostID
114	            ) == id.hostID
115	        }?.value
116	    }
117	
118	    private func activityDate(for card: DockThreadCardDTO) -> Date {
119	        if let activityAtMs = card.activityAtMs {
120	            return Date(timeIntervalSince1970: TimeInterval(activityAtMs) / 1_000)
121	        }
122	        let fractionalFormatter = ISO8601DateFormatter()
123	        fractionalFormatter.formatOptions = [.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds]
124	        if let date = fractionalFormatter.date(from: card.activityAt) {
125	            return date
126	        }
127	        if let date = ISO8601DateFormatter().date(from: card.activityAt) {
128	            return date
129	        }

171	        guard date != .distantPast else {
172	            return "No activity"
173	        }
174	        let seconds = max(0, Int(now().timeIntervalSince(date)))
175	
176	        switch seconds {
177	        case 0..<60:
178	            return "now"
179	        case 60..<3_600:
180	            return "\(seconds / 60)m ago"
181	        case 3_600..<86_400:

173	            rail: try container.decodeIfPresent(DockRowRail.self, forKey: .rail),
174	            isPinned: try container.decodeIfPresent(Bool.self, forKey: .isPinned) ?? false,
175	            pinnedAt: try container.decodeIfPresent(Date.self, forKey: .pinnedAt),
176	            pinnedOrder: try container.decodeIfPresent(Int.self, forKey: .pinnedOrder),
177	            lastKnownPinnedDisplay: try container.decodeIfPresent(
178	                LocalPinnedDisplaySnapshot.self,
179	                forKey: .lastKnownPinnedDisplay
180	            )
181	        )
182	    }
183	
184	    public func encode(to encoder: Encoder) throws {
185	        var container = encoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
186	        try container.encodeIfPresent(label, forKey: .label)
187	        try container.encodeIfPresent(rail, forKey: .rail)
188	        try container.encode(isPinned, forKey: .isPinned)
189	        try container.encodeIfPresent(pinnedAt, forKey: .pinnedAt)
190	        try container.encodeIfPresent(pinnedOrder, forKey: .pinnedOrder)
191	        try container.encodeIfPresent(lastKnownPinnedDisplay, forKey: .lastKnownPinnedDisplay)
192	    }
193	}
194	
195	public protocol LocalThreadMetadataStoring: Sendable {
196	    func load() async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
197	    func save(
198	        _ metadata: LocalThreadMetadata?,
199	        for key: LocalThreadMetadataKey
200	    ) async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
201	    func save(
202	        _ values: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
203	    ) async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
204	}
205	
206	public actor FileLocalThreadMetadataStore: LocalThreadMetadataStoring {
207	    private struct Entry: Codable {
208	        let key: LocalThreadMetadataKey
209	        let metadata: LocalThreadMetadata
210	    }
211	
212	    private let fileURL: URL
213	    private var cache: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]?
214	
215	    public init(fileURL: URL = FileLocalThreadMetadataStore.defaultFileURL()) {
216	        self.fileURL = fileURL
217	    }
218	
219	    public func load() async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata] {
220	        if let cache {
221	            DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata load cache hit entries=\(cache.count, privacy: .public)")
222	            return cache
223	        }
224	
225	        let loaded: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
226	        if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path) {
227	            DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata load started path=\(self.fileURL.path, privacy: .public)")
228	            let data = try Data(contentsOf: fileURL)
229	            let entries = try JSONDecoder().decode([Entry].self, from: data)
230	            loaded = Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues: entries.map { ($0.key, $0.metadata) })
231	        } else {
232	            loaded = [:]
233	        }
234	        cache = loaded
235	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata load finished entries=\(loaded.count, privacy: .public)")
236	        return loaded
237	    }
238	
239	    public func save(
240	        _ metadata: LocalThreadMetadata?,
241	        for key: LocalThreadMetadataKey
242	    ) async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata] {
243	        var values = try await load()
244	        if let metadata, !metadata.isEmpty {
245	            values[key] = metadata
246	        } else {
247	            values.removeValue(forKey: key)
248	        }
249	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata persist started host_id=\(key.hostID, privacy: .public) thread_id=\(DockLog.publicID(key.threadID), privacy: .public) entries=\(values.count, privacy: .public)")
250	        let persisted = try await save(values)
251	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata persist finished host_id=\(key.hostID, privacy: .public) thread_id=\(DockLog.publicID(key.threadID), privacy: .public) entries=\(persisted.count, privacy: .public)")
252	        return persisted
253	    }
254	
255	    public func save(
256	        _ values: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
257	    ) async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata] {
258	        let persistedValues = values.filter { !$0.value.isEmpty }
259	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata batch persist started entries=\(persistedValues.count, privacy: .public)")
260	        try persist(persistedValues)
261	        cache = persistedValues
262	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata batch persist finished entries=\(persistedValues.count, privacy: .public)")
263	        return persistedValues
264	    }
265	
266	    private func persist(_ values: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]) throws {
267	        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(
268	            at: fileURL.deletingLastPathComponent(),
269	            withIntermediateDirectories: true
270	        )
271	        let entries = values
272	            .map { Entry(key: $0.key, metadata: $0.value) }
273	            .sorted {
274	                [$0.key.hostID, $0.key.backendSessionID, $0.key.threadID].joined(separator: "\u{1f}")
275	                    < [$1.key.hostID, $1.key.backendSessionID, $1.key.threadID].joined(separator: "\u{1f}")
276	            }
277	        let data = try JSONEncoder().encode(entries)
278	        try data.write(to: fileURL, options: [.atomic])
279	    }
280	
281	    public static func defaultFileURL() -> URL {
282	        let directory = FileManager.default.urls(
283	            for: .applicationSupportDirectory,
284	            in: .userDomainMask
285	        ).first ?? FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory
286	        return directory
287	            .appendingPathComponent("CodexDock", isDirectory: true)
288	            .appendingPathComponent("thread-metadata.json")
289	    }
290	}

1	# Codex Dock Relay Data Contract And Lease Drift Audit - 2026-05-31
2	
3	## Bottom Line
4	
5	The drift is real. The generated Dock card contract keeps the JSON payload shape aligned between relay and Swift, but it does not unify the semantic source of truth for activity time, row order, live lease state, host freshness, or turn-level updates.
6	
7	The exact failure mode is: Dock cards are built from thread-level `thread/list` plus `thread/read includeTurns:false`, while current work can live only in `thread/turns/list` or live turn events. Nothing currently promotes those newer turn timestamps into Dock `activityAtMs`, `orderKey`, summary, row freshness, or persisted relay state.
8	
9	## Runtime Evidence From The Current Bug
10	
11	Observed on 2026-05-31:
12	
13	- Active thread: `019e7e7d-66ca-7280-9aa0-2e272f1752b1`.
14	- `thread/read` returned `updatedAt=1780238608`, which is `2026-05-31T14:43:28Z`.
15	- `thread/turns/list` returned newer turns:
16	  - `startedAt=1780249079`, `2026-05-31T17:37:59Z`, status `interrupted`.
17	  - `startedAt=1780246962`, `2026-05-31T17:02:42Z`, status `completed`.
18	- `dock/subscribe` used the stale thread-level activity timestamp, so the card sorted as old even though current turn activity existed.
19	
20	Plain English: the relay did not lose the current work. It was visible on the turn-detail route. The Dock overview simply never looked at that route when creating the card.
21	
22	## What The Existing Generated Contract Actually Protects
23	
24	The canonical card payload shape is `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json`.
25	
26	Line audit:
27	
28	| File | Lines | What it protects | What it does not protect |
29	| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
30	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 6-23 | Every stream update must have `kind`, `schemaVersion`, `view`, `epoch`, and `seq`; schema version is fixed at `2`. | It does not say where `activityAtMs` must come from. |
31	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 30-95 | The stream may carry `complete`, `totalRows`, `window`, `freshness`, hosts, cards, upserts, and deletes. | It does not prove a complete stream inspected turns. |
32	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 97-124 | Old session/message fields are explicitly rejected. | It only rejects obsolete fields; it does not validate semantic freshness. |
33	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 157-191 | Host-level freshness has `unknown`, `fresh`, `stale`, `offline`, `error`. | It does not define row-level freshness behavior during retained stale rows. |
34	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 223-240 | Card required fields include `orderKey`, `activityAt`, `displaySummary`, `title`, `status`, `sourceKind`, `lane`, `archiveState`, `freshness`, and `completeness`. | It requires these fields to exist, not to be derived from the latest real work. |
35	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 269-282 | `orderKey`, `activityAt`, and optional `activityAtMs` exist in the payload. | It does not say whether order uses list ordinal, thread `updatedAt`, latest turn time, or lease time. |
36	| `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift` | 1-2 | Swift DTO is generated from that schema. | Generated Swift mirrors shape only. |
37	| `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift` | 342-365 | Swift decodes the card fields exactly as the relay sends them. | Swift has no second source for newer card activity. |
38	| `scripts/generate-dock-thread-card-contract.mjs` | 500-518 | `npm run contract:check` fails if generated Swift is stale. | The generator cannot detect bad source selection inside relay projection. |
39	
40	Net: we made payload-shape drift hard. We did not make data-source drift hard.
41	
42	## Exhaustive Contract Surface Map
43	
44	This section is the missing contract map. It separates three things that had
45	been blurred together:
46	
47	1. The source that owns data.
48	2. The endpoint that exposes or transforms that data.
49	3. The app or script that consumes that endpoint.
50	
51	The important point: the generated `DockThreadCard` contract covers only the
52	card stream shape. It does not cover every source, every relay route, or every
53	consumer that can affect what the user sees.
54	
55	### Data Planes
56	
57	| Plane | What it is | Primary owners | Primary consumers | Contract status |
58	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
59	| Raw Codex history | The app-server at `historyUrl`; relay reads it through pooled JSON-RPC. | `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs:38-48`, `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs:552-566` | Relay `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/search`, `thread/goal/get`, Dock reconcile | Not covered by `DockThreadCard`; raw `ThreadDTO`/list/detail shapes. |
60	| Live upstream sessions | Current app-server sessions found through `thread/loaded/list` and `thread/read`. | `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs:92-120`, `scripts/dock-relay-live-status-cache.mjs:94-153` | `SessionRouter`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/resume`, live leases | Not covered except when projected into a card stream. |
61	| Relay SQLite projection | `.codex-dock/relay-state.sqlite`; stores projected cards, sync scopes, changes, and live leases. | `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs:124-195`, `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs:535-620` | `dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, `dock/resync`, `archive/*`, diagnostics | Card rows are covered after projection; DB-only fields are not. |
62	| Generated card contract | JSON schema plus generated Swift DTO for card stream updates. | `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json`, `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift` | Dock, Archive, cleanup, snapshot loader | Covers shape, enum vocabulary, stream version, and required fields. Does not cover freshness source. |
63	| Swift local metadata | User-owned local pin/label/rail display state. | `CodexDock/State/LocalThreadMetadataStore.swift:3-120`, `CodexDock/Metadata/LocalMetadataEngine.swift:83-105` | Dock projection, Archive, Archive cleanup | Not covered; it is a local overlay keyed by card identity. |
64	| Detail/live event stream | Raw thread turns, notifications, and server requests after opening a thread. | `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:563-625`, `scripts/dock-relay.mjs:446-524` | Thread Detail, composer, request cards | Not covered by `DockThreadCard`; mostly `ThreadDTO`, turn DTOs, and raw `JSONValue`. |
65	| Observability | Route health, traces, metrics, status snapshots. | `scripts/dock-relay-observability.mjs`, `scripts/dock-relay-status.mjs` | Connectivity UI, diagnostics, Makefile targets, audits | Not a data contract for rows. |
66	| Voice transcription | Relay-owned realtime transcription bridge. | `scripts/dock-relay-realtime-transcription.mjs`, `CodexDock/AppServer/RealtimeTranscriptionDTO.swift` | Voice composer | Separate voice contract; no Dock card authority. |

178	### Undocumented Contract Gaps
179	
180	These are the places where the current data contract lets the system drift:
181	
182	1. `activityAt` has no canonical source. It might come from `thread.activityAt`, `thread.updatedAt`, `thread.createdAt`, list ordinal, or a cached row. The schema only requires the field to exist.
183	2. `orderKey` has no semantic rule. Active Dock uses list ordinal order; Archive uses activity-derived order; the client may sort again by local activity date.
184	3. `displaySummary` has no freshness rule. It can be derived from thread-level metadata even when newer turn content exists.
185	4. `thread/turns/list` is the detail source for newest work, but the card stream contract does not require Dock cards to inspect it.
186	5. Live leases are status overlays only. They do not carry or repair `activityAt`, `orderKey`, `title`, `displaySummary`, repo, branch, or working directory.
187	6. `LiveStatusCache` and SQLite `live_leases` have separate lifecycles. Detail routing can disagree with Dock lease overlay.
188	7. Host freshness is scope-level. A host can be stale while rows remain visible, and a row can look fresh while its semantic source is stale.
189	8. Local pin metadata is a separate display cache. It can keep a pinned row visible with old title/status/activity when no current card exists.
190	9. `relay/state/snapshot`, `state/query`, `/statez`, `/syncz`, `/explainz`, and parity scripts are useful truth/oracle surfaces, but they are not the app card contract.
191	10. Route health is not row freshness. `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`, and traces can be green while card ordering is wrong.
192	11. Thread Detail has its own raw event/request contract. Request cards and turn events can drift independently from `DockThreadCard`.
193	12. Contract checks protect only a small fixture set and generated Swift text. They do not run full JSON Schema validation against broad runtime examples.

325	## Drift Inventory
326	
327	| Drift point | Root cause | User-visible result |
328	| --- | --- | --- |
329	| Current turn activity not on top | Dock never reads `thread/turns/list` during card reconcile. | A thread with active recent work appears old. |
330	| Old card summary/title | Summary comes from thread row fields, not latest turn content. | Card text can lag behind current conversation. |
331	| `orderKey` vs activity | Active Dock `orderKey` is list ordinal. | Store ordering can preserve stale list order. |
332	| `activityAtMs` vs turn timestamps | `activityAtMs` is projected from `activityAt` or thread `updatedAt/createdAt`. | Client cannot sort by real newest work if relay timestamp is stale. |
333	| Lease status vs card data | Leases update status/session only. | A live-looking card can still have old title/activity. |
334	| Expired lease edge | Expired lease only downgrades dormant cards. | A stored `running` status can survive lease expiry. |
335	| Live detail route vs Dock lease route | `LiveStatusCache` and `refreshLiveLeases` use different timing/source sets. | Detail and Dock can disagree about what is live. |
336	| Host freshness vs row freshness | `freshnessForHost` is scope-based; rows are retained. | UI can show data while also saying partial/stale. |
337	| Route health vs data freshness | Route observability measures request outcome, not payload semantic age. | `/readyz` or route health can look OK while Dock data is stale. |
338	| Generated schema confidence | Schema validates shape, not source semantics. | `contract:check` can pass while user-facing ordering is wrong. |

342	These tests are useful guardrails, but several of them encode the behavior that makes the current bug possible:
343	
344	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:206` - stale scope keeps existing rows visible.
345	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:243` - live lease publishes status-only card changes.
346	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:292` - expired lease behavior is tested for the dormant case.
347	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:628` - fresh cached `dock/subscribe` can skip refresh.
348	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:1280` - Dock card activity comes from thread fields.
349	- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:190` - `/readyz` can pass while Dock state freshness is stale.
350	- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:238` - `dock/subscribe` route health can be healthy while serving stale cached state.
351	- `CodexDockTests/DockStoreStreamTests.swift:219` - stale heartbeat retains rows as partial.
352	- `CodexDockTests/ThreadDetailStoreTests.swift:5` and related tests - detail store relies on `thread/turns/list`, which is separate from Dock cards.
353	- `CodexDockTests/DockRenderProjectorTests.swift:44` - cached pinned rows can render without live cards.
354	
355	## What Would Make Drift Actually Hard
356	
357	This is not an implementation plan, just the architectural conclusion from the audit.
358	
359	The contract would need to define a canonical activity source, not just fields:
360	
361	1. Dock card recency must mean "latest user-visible thread activity", with a precise priority order such as latest turn timestamp, then live event timestamp, then thread `updatedAt`, then `createdAt`.
362	2. Relay state must persist that canonical activity timestamp separately from list ordinal and raw `updatedAt`.
363	3. `orderKey` must be derived from canonical activity, or the client must ignore relay order for global recency.
364	4. Live leases must either remain a status-only overlay by contract, or explicitly carry activity/summary fields and a freshness source.
365	5. Route health must not be presented as data freshness. `/readyz` remains process proof only.
366	6. The generated schema should be extended only if the semantic source can be enforced or tested; otherwise it will keep giving false confidence.
367	
368	## Verdict
369	
370	The relay/client contract is not "impossible to drift." It is shape-safe but source-unsafe.
371	
372	The current user-facing bug is not primarily a Swift display bug. Swift is faithfully displaying stale card fields. The deeper bug is in the relay Dock projection: it treats thread-level rows as canonical for overview recency while the real current work can exist only in turn-level data.

3	struct DockRenderProjector: Sendable {

5	
6	    init(now: @escaping @Sendable () -> Date = Date.init) {

11	        from input: DockRenderInput,

13	    ) -> DockSnapshot {
14	        let rowProjector = ThreadCardRowProjector(
15	            hosts: input.hosts,
16	            hostIdentityResolver: input.hostIdentityResolver,
17	            localMetadata: localMetadata,
18	            now: now
19	        )
20	        let liveRows = input.hosts.flatMap { host in
21	            rowProjector.rows(
22	                from: input.cardsByHostID[host.id] ?? [],
23	                sourceHostID: host.id
24	            )
25	        }
26	        let loadedKeys = Set(liveRows.map(\.metadataKey))
27	        let rows = liveRows + rowProjector.cachedPinnedRows(excluding: loadedKeys)
28	
29	        return DockSnapshot(
30	            host: DockHostViewModel(host: input.hosts[0]),
31	            hosts: input.hosts.map(DockHostViewModel.init),
32	            hostStates: input.hostStates,
33	            hostIdentityResolver: input.hostIdentityResolver,
34	            rows: rows,
35	            isPartial: input.isPartial
36	        )
37	    }

39	    func render(
40	        snapshot: DockSnapshot,
41	        options: DockProjectionOptions,
42	        revision: RenderRevision
43	    ) -> DockRenderSnapshot {
44	        DockRenderSnapshot(
45	            revision: revision,
46	            snapshot: snapshot,
47	            projection: snapshot.project(options: options)
48	        )

1	# Codex Dock Connectivity Detection And Display Audit - 2026-05-31
2	
3	## Bottom Line
4	
5	Connectivity detection is broad, but the display can overstate health. The app collects Dock, Archive, Relay Settings, Thread Detail, route diagnostics, and lifecycle evidence, then rolls it into one status. The problem is that `.partial` is treated as "online-like", so degraded hosts can produce labels like `Online 2/2`.
6	
7	Plain English: the app often knows something is degraded, but the small top badge can make that feel healthier than it is.
8	
9	## High-Level Model
10	
11	Codex Dock has two health layers:
12	
13	1. Swift app connectivity: local stores report host state into `AppConnectivityStore` or `ConnectivityEventSink`.
14	2. Node relay health: HTTP endpoints and route observability report process health, route health, app-critical failures, and relay state.
15	
16	These are related but not identical. `/readyz` proves the relay process can answer. It does not prove Dock card data is fresh.
17	
18	## Swift App Reporting Paths
19	
20	Line audit:
21	
22	| File | Lines | Behavior | UX implication |
23	| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
24	| `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift` | 250-257 | In the non-runtime path, Dock, Archive, and Hosts stores report directly to `AppConnectivityStore`. | Store state goes straight into the global badge. |
25	| `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift` | 495-515 | Dock store either reports directly or emits `ConnectivityRuntimeEvent`s. | Dock stream state is a first-class connectivity input. |
26	| `CodexDock/State/ArchiveStore.swift` | 279-339 | Archive store uses the same pattern and maps host states to connectivity phases. | Archive can influence global status. |
27	| `CodexDock/State/HostSettingsStore.swift` | 297-319 | Manual host tests emit connectivity facts. | Settings tests can change app health display. |
28	| `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift` | 818-850 | Thread detail maps live state to checking, reconnecting, online, stale, or offline. | Opening a thread can update global host health. |
29	| `CodexDock/Runtime/ConnectivityEventSink.swift` | 13-37 | Runtime events carry source, host id, route, status, phase, and timestamp. | Multiple app areas can feed one health stream. |
30	| `CodexDock/Connectivity/ConnectivityDataEngine.swift` | 25-43 | Runtime events update host records and last success when phase is online-like. | `.partial` can update success timing because it is online-like. |
31	
32	## AppConnectivityStore State Rules
33	
34	Line audit:
35	
36	| File | Lines | Behavior | UX implication |
37	| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
38	| `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift` | 4-15 | Host phases are `unknown`, `checking`, `online`, `partial`, `reconnecting`, `backgrounded`, `resuming`, `stale`, `offline`, `error`, and `configurationError`. | The model has enough vocabulary to represent degraded states. |
39	| `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift` | 17-26 | `isOnlineLike` returns true for `.online` and `.partial`. | This is the key reason degraded hosts can count as online. |
40	| `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift` | 76-113 | Overall labels include `Online`, `Partial`, `Stale`, `Offline`, `Error`, and `Config error`. | The model can say partial/stale, but the badge may choose count wording. |
41	| `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift` | 275-293 | Dock store state is converted into host observations. | Dock stream stale/incomplete states flow into connectivity. |
42	| `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift` | 296-310 | Archive state is converted using the same host-state model. | Archive and Dock share status vocabulary. |
43	| `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift` | 313-330 | Manual host test state becomes online/offline/error/checking. | Manual tests can make a host look online even if Dock data is stale. |
44	| `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift` | 527-540 | Host snapshot prefers lifecycle phase, then route diagnostic phase, then store observations. | Background/resume and route failures can override normal store reports. |
45	| `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift` | 543-548 | App-critical failed route becomes `.partial("<route> failed")`. | Critical route failure is degraded, not hard offline/error. |
46	| `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift` | 550-557 | Multiple observations roll up by priority. | One stale/detail event can beat an online Dock event for that host. |
47	| `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift` | 559-635 | Overall rollup chooses global app status. | The final badge is a rollup, not a direct relay truth. |
48	| `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift` | 594-618 | `onlineLikeCount` includes partial hosts. | This is where `Online N/N` can include degraded hosts. |
49	| `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift` | 637-650 | Priority ranks stale above checking/offline/error/partial/online. | Stale should win inside one host if it is reported as stale, but many Dock stale rows are mapped to partial before this point. |
50	
51	## Dock Store Connectivity Mapping
52	
53	Line audit:
54	
55	| File | Lines | Behavior | UX implication |
56	| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
57	| `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift` | 58-64 | Reconnecting with retained rows becomes `.partial(rowCount, "Reconnecting")`. | Existing rows stay visible and host appears partial. |
58	| `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift` | 67-80 | Offline/error with retained rows becomes partial instead of unavailable. | Data stays visible, but global badge may still count host online-like. |
59	| `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift` | 82-112 | Snapshot freshness and completeness become host status. | Relay freshness drives Dock host state. |
60	| `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift` | 115-168 | Updates preserve latest freshness/complete/window and recompute host status. | Stale heartbeats can keep rows and mark partial. |
61	| `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift` | 321-350 | Incomplete windows and stale freshness map to `.partial`; offline/error map to partial if rows exist. | Retained rows are degraded, not hidden. |
62	| `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift` | 517-585 | Dock state emits connectivity events for configuration, loading, offline, error, and loaded host states. | The top badge follows Dock stream host states. |
63	| `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift` | 588-605 | `DockHostLoadStatus.partial` becomes `HostConnectivityPhase.partial`. | Partial is later counted as online-like. |
64	
65	## Thread Detail Connectivity Mapping
66	
67	Line audit:
68	
69	| File | Lines | Behavior | UX implication |
70	| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
71	| `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift` | 38-55 | Detail live states are `connecting`, `reconnecting`, `live`, `stale`, and `closed`. | Detail has a clearer stale/live model than Dock card rows. |
72	| `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift` | 476-499 | Backgrounding a loaded live detail marks it stale with message `Backgrounded`. | Background state is explicit. |
73	| `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift` | 501-523 | Foreground resume rehydrates if connected, waits if reconnecting, or marks stale. | Resume state can temporarily override health. |
74	| `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift` | 818-850 | Detail publishes checking, reconnecting, online, stale, and offline phases. | Detail stale can correctly become global stale when it wins the rollup. |
75	
76	## Global Badge Display
77	
78	Line audit:
79	
80	| File | Lines | Behavior | UX implication |
81	| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
82	| `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift` | 400-416 | The Dock header renders `GlobalConnectivityIndicatorView`. | This is the small badge the user sees first. |
83	| `CodexDock/Features/Status/GlobalConnectivityIndicatorView.swift` | 44-68 | Display label is chosen from overall status. | `.partial` does not always display as `Partial`. |
84	| `CodexDock/Features/Status/GlobalConnectivityIndicatorView.swift` | 48-51 | `.online` and `.partial` both use `hostCountLabel(prefix:"Online")` for multi-host. | Multi-host partial can display `Online 2/2`. |
85	| `CodexDock/Features/Status/GlobalConnectivityIndicatorView.swift` | 71-77 | Host count label counts hosts where `phase.isOnlineLike`. | Since `.partial` is online-like, partial hosts are counted as online. |
86	| `CodexDock/Features/Status/GlobalConnectivityIndicatorView.swift` | 79-101 | Icons distinguish partial/stale/offline/error. | The icon may warn even when text says `Online N/N`. |
87	| `CodexDock/Features/Status/GlobalConnectivityIndicatorView.swift` | 104-114 | Partial/stale/reconnecting/backgrounded/resuming are orange; online is green. | Color can be more accurate than text. |
88	
89	Misleading state:
90	
91	- If both hosts have retained stale rows, the global status can be `.partial`, but the label can say `Online 2/2`.
92	- That matches the simulator symptom where the header says `Online 2/2` while the Dock summary says `Partial`.
93	
94	## System Health Display
95	
96	Line audit:
97	
98	| File | Lines | Behavior | UX implication |
99	| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
100	| `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthView.swift` | 49-58 | `Run check` calls `store.refreshRelayDiagnostics()`. | User can ask for route diagnostics manually. |
101	| `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthView.swift` | 70-81 | Summary card shows `overallStatus.label` and message. | Full sheet is more explicit than the badge. |
102	| `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthView.swift` | 84-105 | Category grid shows category health. | Route evidence is grouped by product area. |
103	| `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthView.swift` | 109-149 | Host cards use `host.phase.isOnlineLike` for checkmark/green vs warning/orange. | Partial hosts can get green checkmarks. |
104	| `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthView.swift` | 225-260 | Host detail lists route evidence and reasons. | The real technical detail exists, but is one tap deeper. |
105	| `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthProjector.swift` | 31-59 | Diagnostics route status maps failed/blocked to failed, degraded/partial/stale to degraded. | Route-level stale is handled. |
106	| `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthProjector.swift` | 62-86 | Fallback status maps overall partial to degraded, stale to stale, offline/error/config to failed. | System Health has better wording than the top badge. |
107	| `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthProjector.swift` | 89-112 | Categories map routes: Dock feed, Thread detail, Archive, Voice, Diagnostics. | Route health is category-based, not card freshness proof. |
108	
109	## Dock Host Context Rows
110	
111	Line audit:
112	
113	| File | Lines | Behavior | UX implication |
114	| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
115	| `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift` | 927-930 | Contextual host rows include checking, partial, and unavailable hosts. | Dock does surface partial host state below rows. |
116	| `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift` | 958-968 | Non-unavailable partial hosts render using `HostLoadingRow`. | Partial rows look like loading/blue rows, not warning rows. |
117	| `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockGroupRows.swift` | 68-92 | `HostLoadingRow` uses blue desktop/checking styling and displays status subtitle. | Degraded partial state can look too calm. |
118	| `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockGroupRows.swift` | 95-125 | `HostFailureRow` has orange warning styling and Retry/Relay actions. | Only unavailable hosts get the stronger visual treatment. |
119	
120	## Relay HTTP Health
121	
122	Line audit:
123	
124	| File | Lines | Behavior | UX implication |
125	| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
126	| `scripts/dock-relay.mjs` | 848-855 | `/readyz` returns `ok:true`, service name, and auth mode. | Process-only proof. Not data freshness. |
127	| `scripts/dock-relay.mjs` | 763-767 | `/statusz` checks raw app-server health then returns relay status. | Better than `/readyz`, but callers must read nested fields. |
128	| `scripts/dock-relay.mjs` | 769-774 | `/metricsz` returns metrics snapshot. | Uses last-known raw health; not a fresh probe by itself. |
129	| `scripts/dock-relay.mjs` | 783-794 | `/routesz` returns route health evidence. | Best route-level diagnostic source. |
130	| `scripts/dock-relay-status.mjs` | 205-260 | `/statusz` includes `routes` and `appCriticalFailures`. | Top-level `ok:true` can coexist with nested failures. |
131	| `scripts/dock-relay-status.mjs` | 263-280 | `/metricsz` includes live status and state counts. | Useful for operators, not directly shown as the top badge. |
132	
133	## Route Diagnostics
134	
135	Line audit:
136	
137	| File | Lines | Behavior | UX implication |
138	| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
139	| `scripts/dock-relay-observability-contract.mjs` | 1-9 | Route statuses are `unknown`, `healthy`, `degraded`, `failed`, `stale`, `partial`, and `blocked`. | Route language is richer than the top badge. |
140	| `scripts/dock-relay-observability-contract.mjs` | 33-79 | Route names include HTTP endpoints, Dock routes, Thread Detail routes, turn routes, and transcription routes. | Diagnostics can be route-specific. |
141	| `scripts/dock-relay-observability-contract.mjs` | 192-258 | `initialize`, `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, etc. are app-critical as configured. | Critical route failures should matter to UX. |
142	| `scripts/dock-relay-observability-contract.mjs` | 273-320 | Dock and Archive stream routes are app-critical. | Stream health is tracked separately from data freshness. |
143	| `scripts/dock-relay-observability-contract.mjs` | 328-370 | Turn and transcription routes are app-critical/passive. | Live work routes can be unhealthy independently of Dock cards. |
144	| `scripts/dock-relay-observability.mjs` | 219-239 | Route records include schema, route, appCritical, status reasons, counters, and impact. | The evidence model is good. |
145	| `scripts/dock-relay-observability.mjs` | 291-355 | Active operations start as partial. | In-flight route work is not yet success or failure. |
146	| `scripts/dock-relay-observability.mjs` | 358-375 | Finished operations update route outcome from request result. | Successful stale payloads can still be route-successful. |
147	| `scripts/dock-relay-observability.mjs` | 514-516 | `appCriticalFailures` only includes failed routes. | Stale/degraded route evidence may not trigger the strongest UI language. |
148	
149	## UX Mismatch Inventory
150	
151	| Mismatch | Root cause | What the user sees |
152	| --- | --- | --- |
153	| `Online 2/2` while Dock is partial | `.partial` is `isOnlineLike`, and the badge uses online-like count. | Header sounds healthy even with retained stale rows. |
154	| Green check for partial host in System Health | Host card icon checks `phase.isOnlineLike`. | A degraded host can look healthy. |
155	| Blue partial host rows in Dock | Partial-but-available rows render via `HostLoadingRow`. | Degraded state looks like neutral loading. |
156	| `/readyz` passes while Dock is stale | `/readyz` is process-only. | Operator may think relay is fine when app data is stale. |
157	| Route health healthy while payload stale | Observability tracks request success, not semantic payload freshness. | System can say route worked even when data is old. |
158	| Dock partial state counted as success timestamp | `.partial` is online-like. | Last success can advance on degraded evidence. |
159	
160	## Tests That Encode Current Behavior
161	
162	- `CodexDockTests/AppConnectivityStoreTests.swift:16` - Dock online rolls up as online.
163	- `CodexDockTests/AppConnectivityStoreTests.swift:39` - all loading rolls up as checking.
164	- `CodexDockTests/AppConnectivityStoreTests.swift:51` - loaded plus checking rolls up as partial.
165	- `CodexDockTests/AppConnectivityStoreTests.swift:78` - partial host rolls up as partial.
166	- `CodexDockTests/AppConnectivityStoreTests.swift:171` - app-critical route failure overrides process evidence as partial.
167	- `CodexDockTests/AppConnectivityStoreTests.swift:285` - lifecycle masks old facts until active.
168	- `CodexDockTests/ConnectivityDataEngineTests.swift:5` - runtime events update connectivity.
169	- `CodexDockTests/SystemHealthProjectorTests.swift:5` - healthy Dock with passive categories not checked.
170	- `CodexDockTests/SystemHealthProjectorTests.swift:30` - app-critical failure maps failed.
171	- `CodexDockTests/SystemHealthProjectorTests.swift:60` - partial route maps degraded.
172	- `CodexDockTests/DockStoreStreamTests.swift:219` - stale heartbeat retains rows as partial.
173	- `CodexDockTests/DockStoreStreamTests.swift:333` - windowed snapshot is explicitly partial.
174	- `CodexDockTests/DockStoreStreamTests.swift:478` - closed stream retains rows as partial/offline.
175	- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:190` - `/readyz` can pass while Dock state is stale.
176	- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:238` - stale cached `dock/subscribe` can still leave route health healthy.
177	
178	## Verdict
179	
180	This is both a technical and UX mismatch, not just a wording issue.
181	
182	Technically, the app collects enough evidence to know "degraded but usable" versus "fully healthy." UX-wise, the header badge and some host rows collapse that distinction by treating partial as online-like. That makes the current relay/card staleness bugs feel more confusing because the user sees old work while the app still says some form of "Online."

1	# Codex Dock Relay Data Contract And Lease Drift Audit - 2026-05-31
2	
3	## Bottom Line
4	
5	The drift is real. The generated Dock card contract keeps the JSON payload shape aligned between relay and Swift, but it does not unify the semantic source of truth for activity time, row order, live lease state, host freshness, or turn-level updates.
6	
7	The exact failure mode is: Dock cards are built from thread-level `thread/list` plus `thread/read includeTurns:false`, while current work can live only in `thread/turns/list` or live turn events. Nothing currently promotes those newer turn timestamps into Dock `activityAtMs`, `orderKey`, summary, row freshness, or persisted relay state.
8	
9	## Runtime Evidence From The Current Bug
10	
11	Observed on 2026-05-31:
12	
13	- Active thread: `019e7e7d-66ca-7280-9aa0-2e272f1752b1`.
14	- `thread/read` returned `updatedAt=1780238608`, which is `2026-05-31T14:43:28Z`.
15	- `thread/turns/list` returned newer turns:
16	  - `startedAt=1780249079`, `2026-05-31T17:37:59Z`, status `interrupted`.
17	  - `startedAt=1780246962`, `2026-05-31T17:02:42Z`, status `completed`.
18	- `dock/subscribe` used the stale thread-level activity timestamp, so the card sorted as old even though current turn activity existed.
19	
20	Plain English: the relay did not lose the current work. It was visible on the turn-detail route. The Dock overview simply never looked at that route when creating the card.
21	
22	## What The Existing Generated Contract Actually Protects
23	
24	The canonical card payload shape is `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json`.
25	
26	Line audit:
27	
28	| File | Lines | What it protects | What it does not protect |
29	| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
30	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 6-23 | Every stream update must have `kind`, `schemaVersion`, `view`, `epoch`, and `seq`; schema version is fixed at `2`. | It does not say where `activityAtMs` must come from. |
31	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 30-95 | The stream may carry `complete`, `totalRows`, `window`, `freshness`, hosts, cards, upserts, and deletes. | It does not prove a complete stream inspected turns. |
32	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 97-124 | Old session/message fields are explicitly rejected. | It only rejects obsolete fields; it does not validate semantic freshness. |
33	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 157-191 | Host-level freshness has `unknown`, `fresh`, `stale`, `offline`, `error`. | It does not define row-level freshness behavior during retained stale rows. |
34	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 223-240 | Card required fields include `orderKey`, `activityAt`, `displaySummary`, `title`, `status`, `sourceKind`, `lane`, `archiveState`, `freshness`, and `completeness`. | It requires these fields to exist, not to be derived from the latest real work. |
35	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 269-282 | `orderKey`, `activityAt`, and optional `activityAtMs` exist in the payload. | It does not say whether order uses list ordinal, thread `updatedAt`, latest turn time, or lease time. |
36	| `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift` | 1-2 | Swift DTO is generated from that schema. | Generated Swift mirrors shape only. |
37	| `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift` | 342-365 | Swift decodes the card fields exactly as the relay sends them. | Swift has no second source for newer card activity. |
38	| `scripts/generate-dock-thread-card-contract.mjs` | 500-518 | `npm run contract:check` fails if generated Swift is stale. | The generator cannot detect bad source selection inside relay projection. |
39	
40	Net: we made payload-shape drift hard. We did not make data-source drift hard.
41	
42	## Exhaustive Contract Surface Map
43	
44	This section is the missing contract map. It separates three things that had
45	been blurred together:
46	
47	1. The source that owns data.
48	2. The endpoint that exposes or transforms that data.
49	3. The app or script that consumes that endpoint.
50	
51	The important point: the generated `DockThreadCard` contract covers only the
52	card stream shape. It does not cover every source, every relay route, or every
53	consumer that can affect what the user sees.
54	
55	### Data Planes
56	
57	| Plane | What it is | Primary owners | Primary consumers | Contract status |
58	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
59	| Raw Codex history | The app-server at `historyUrl`; relay reads it through pooled JSON-RPC. | `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs:38-48`, `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs:552-566` | Relay `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/search`, `thread/goal/get`, Dock reconcile | Not covered by `DockThreadCard`; raw `ThreadDTO`/list/detail shapes. |
60	| Live upstream sessions | Current app-server sessions found through `thread/loaded/list` and `thread/read`. | `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs:92-120`, `scripts/dock-relay-live-status-cache.mjs:94-153` | `SessionRouter`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/resume`, live leases | Not covered except when projected into a card stream. |
61	| Relay SQLite projection | `.codex-dock/relay-state.sqlite`; stores projected cards, sync scopes, changes, and live leases. | `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs:124-195`, `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs:535-620` | `dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, `dock/resync`, `archive/*`, diagnostics | Card rows are covered after projection; DB-only fields are not. |
62	| Generated card contract | JSON schema plus generated Swift DTO for card stream updates. | `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json`, `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift` | Dock, Archive, cleanup, snapshot loader | Covers shape, enum vocabulary, stream version, and required fields. 178	### Undocumented Contract Gaps
179	
180	These are the places where the current data contract lets the system drift:
181	
182	1. `activityAt` has no canonical source. It might come from `thread.activityAt`, `thread.updatedAt`, `thread.createdAt`, list ordinal, or a cached row. The schema only requires the field to exist.
183	2. `orderKey` has no semantic rule. Active Dock uses list ordinal order; Archive uses activity-derived order; the client may sort again by local activity date.
184	3. `displaySummary` has no freshness rule. It can be derived from thread-level metadata even when newer turn content exists.
185	4. `thread/turns/list` is the detail source for newest work, but the card stream contract does not require Dock cards to inspect it.
186	5. Live leases are status overlays only. They do not carry or repair `activityAt`, `orderKey`, `title`, `displaySummary`, repo, branch, or working directory.
187	6. `LiveStatusCache` and SQLite `live_leases` have separate lifecycles. Detail routing can disagree with Dock lease overlay.
188	7. Host freshness is scope-level. A host can be stale while rows remain visible, and a row can look fresh while its semantic source is stale.
189	8. Local pin metadata is a separate display cache. It can keep a pinned row visible with old title/status/activity when no current card exists.
190	9. `relay/state/snapshot`, `state/query`, `/statez`, `/syncz`, `/explainz`, and parity scripts are useful truth/oracle surfaces, but they are not the app card contract.
191	10. Route health is not row freshness. `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`, and traces can be green while card ordering is wrong.
192	11. Thread Detail has its own raw event/request contract. Request cards and turn events can drift independently from `DockThreadCard`.
193	12. Contract checks protect only a small fixture set and generated Swift text. They do not run full JSON Schema validation against broad runtime examples.

323	| `scripts/dock-relay-observability.mjs` | 514-516 | `appCriticalFailures` only includes routes with `routeStatus == failed`. | Stale/incomplete data may not become an app-critical failure. |
324	
325	## Drift Inventory
326	
327	| Drift point | Root cause | User-visible result |
328	| --- | --- | --- |
329	| Current turn activity not on top | Dock never reads `thread/turns/list` during card reconcile. | A thread with active recent work appears old. |
330	| Old card summary/title | Summary comes from thread row fields, not latest turn content. | Card text can lag behind current conversation. |
331	| `orderKey` vs activity | Active Dock `orderKey` is list ordinal. | Store ordering can preserve stale list order. |
332	| `activityAtMs` vs turn timestamps | `activityAtMs` is projected from `activityAt` or thread `updatedAt/createdAt`. | Client cannot sort by real newest work if relay timestamp is stale. |
333	| Lease status vs card data | Leases update status/session only. | A live-looking card can still have old title/activity. |
334	| Expired lease edge | Expired lease only downgrades dormant cards. | A stored `running` status can survive lease expiry. |
335	| Live detail route vs Dock lease route | `LiveStatusCache` and `refreshLiveLeases` use different timing/source sets. | Detail and Dock can disagree about what is live. |
336	| Host freshness vs row freshness | `freshnessForHost` is scope-based; rows are retained. | UI can show data while also saying partial/stale. |
337	| Route health vs data freshness | Route observability measures request outcome, not payload semantic age. | `/readyz` or route health can look OK while Dock data is stale. |
338	| Generated schema confidence | Schema validates shape, not source semantics. | `contract:check` can pass while user-facing ordering is wrong. |
339	
340	## Tests That Encode Current Behavior
341	
342	These tests are useful guardrails, but several of them encode the behavior that makes the current bug possible:
343	
344	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:206` - stale scope keeps existing rows visible.
345	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:243` - live lease publishes status-only card changes.
346	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:292` - expired lease behavior is tested for the dormant case.
347	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:628` - fresh cached `dock/subscribe` can skip refresh.
348	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:1280` - Dock card activity comes from thread fields.
349	- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:190` - `/readyz` can pass while Dock state freshness is stale.
350	- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:238` - `dock/subscribe` route health can be healthy while serving stale cached state.
351	- `CodexDockTests/DockStoreStreamTests.swift:219` - stale heartbeat retains rows as partial.
352	- `CodexDockTests/ThreadDetailStoreTests.swift:5` and related tests - detail store relies on `thread/turns/list`, which is separate from Dock cards.
353	- `CodexDockTests/DockRenderProjectorTests.swift:44` - cached pinned rows can render without live cards.
354	
355	## What Would Make Drift Actually Hard
356	
357	This is not an implementation plan, just the architectural conclusion from the audit.
358	
359	The contract would need to define a canonical activity source, not just fields:
360	
361	1. Dock card recency must mean "latest user-visible thread activity", with a precise priority order such as latest turn timestamp, then live event timestamp, then thread `updatedAt`, then `createdAt`.
362	2. Relay state must persist that canonical activity timestamp separately from list ordinal and raw `updatedAt`.
363	3. `orderKey` must be derived from canonical activity, or the client must ignore relay order for global recency.
364	4. Live leases must either remain a status-only overlay by contract, or explicitly carry activity/summary fields and a freshness source.
365	5. Route health must not be presented as data freshness. `/readyz` remains process proof only.
366	6. The generated schema should be extended only if the semantic source can be enforced or tested; otherwise it will keep giving false confidence.
367	
368	## Verdict
369	
370	The relay/client contract is not "impossible to drift." It is shape-safe but source-unsafe.
371	
372	The current user-facing bug is not primarily a Swift display bug. Swift is faithfully displaying stale card fields. The deeper bug is in the relay Dock projection: it treats thread-level rows as canonical for overview recency while the real current work can exist only in turn-level data.
373

501	private func makeSnapshot(
502	    rows: [DockRowViewModel],
503	    hosts: [DockHostConfiguration] = [makeProjectionHost()],
504	    hostStates: [DockHostStateViewModel]? = nil,
505	    isPartial: Bool = false
506	) -> DockSnapshot {
507	    let hostViewModels = hosts.map(DockHostViewModel.init)
508	    let observations = rows.compactMap { row -> DockHostIdentityObservation? in
509	        let sourceHost = row.sourceHostID.flatMap { sourceHostID in
510	            hosts.first { $0.id == sourceHostID }
511	        }
512	        let inferredHost = sourceHost ?? hosts.first { host in
513	            host.id == row.id.hostID
514	                || host.displayName == row.id.hostID
515	                || host.endpoint.displayEndpoint == row.id.hostID
516	        }
517	        guard let host = inferredHost else {
518	            return nil
519	        }
520	        return DockHostIdentityObservation(
521	            configuredHostID: host.id,
522	            logicalHostID: row.id.hostID,
523	            displayName: row.hostDisplayName,
524	            endpoint: row.hostEndpoint
525	        )
526	    }
527	    let resolver = DockHostIdentityResolver(hosts: hosts, observations: observations)
528	    return DockSnapshot(
529	        host: hostViewModels[0],
530	        hosts: hostViewModels,
531	        hostStates: hostStates ?? hosts.map { host in
532	            DockHostStateViewModel(host: DockHostViewModel(host: host), status: .loaded(rowCount: rows.filter { $0.id.hostID == host.id }.count))
533	        },
534	        hostIdentityResolver: resolver,
535	        rows: rows,
536	        isPartial: isPartial
537	    )
538	}

1	# Codex Dock Staleness Root Cause Worklog - 2026-05-31
2	
3	## Goal
4	
5	Root cause why the simulator and phone can stop staying up to date while still looking connected. The concrete symptom under investigation is a Dock list whose latest visible message can show old activity such as `2h ago`.
6	
7	No implementation fixes in this pass. Testing and evidence capture are allowed.
8	
9	## Worklog
10	
11	### 2026-05-31T17:03:20Z - Investigation started
12	
13	- Current repo has existing Swift changes from the Dock ordering fix:
14	  - `CodexDock/State/DockCardProjection.swift`
15	  - `CodexDockTests/DockStoreTestsProjection.swift`
16	- Existing untracked mockup directories are present and unrelated:
17	  - `docs/mockups/codex-dock-conversation-time-order-2026-05-31/`
18	  - `docs/mockups/codex-dock-time-order-2026-05-31/`
19	- The investigation is now focused on freshness/staleness architecture, not ordering.
20	- Initial search found repo-owned sync proof tooling in the `Makefile` and freshness language in `README.md`.
21	
22	### 2026-05-31T17:03-17:05Z - Current simulator and relay evidence captured
23	
24	Artifacts saved under `/tmp/codex-client/staleness-root-cause-20260531/`.
25	
26	- `sim-current.png`: simulator visibly shows:
27	  - global badge: `Online 2/2`
28	  - summary text includes `Partial`
29	  - top visible Dock row: `2h ago`
30	- `sim-log-last-30m.txt` and `sim-log-signal-tail.txt`: app logs repeatedly show stale rows retained:
31	  - `dock stream rows retained host_id=home.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510 freshness=stale rows=961`
32	  - `dock stream rows retained host_id=amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510 freshness=stale rows=188`
33	  - `dock render input exceeds main publish row budget rows=1149 budget=600`
34	- `dock-subscribe-combined.json`: direct `dock/subscribe` probes returned:
35	  - `amir`: `freshness.status=stale`, `complete=true`, `totalRows=188`, `lastError=human-started thread validation failed`, top activity `2026-05-31T14:56:09.000Z`
36	  - `home`: `freshness.status=stale`, `complete=false`, `totalRows=961`, `lastError=websocket closed: ws://127.0.0.1:4500/`, top activity `2026-05-30T16:28:28.000Z`
37	- `/statusz` snapshots for both relays report raw app-server health as `up` and relay service `ok=true`, so transport/service health is not enough to prove Dock freshness.
38	
39	### 2026-05-31T17:04-17:07Z - Immediate stale reasons
40	
41	- Amir relay is repeatedly failing human-started thread validation during Dock reconciliation.
42	  - Relay log event: `human_started_thread.session_index_validation_failed`
43	  - Upstream error example: `thread/read: thread not loaded: 019e0fce-24e5-7471-b971-85b74d72ecf2`
44	  - Reconcile result: `state.reconcile_incomplete` with `validationFailures=14`
45	- Home relay recovered during a later periodic reconcile.
46	  - Relay log event: `state.reconcile_succeeded`
47	  - Rows: `961`
48	  - Validation failures: `0`
49	- This means the repro is not a simple dead relay. At least one relay can be serving a WebSocket connection and cached rows while its Dock freshness is stale or recently recovered.
50	
51	### 2026-05-31T17:05-17:09Z - Client architecture path identified
52	
53	- The client intentionally retains rows when a stream update says freshness is stale.
54	  - `ThreadCardTable.hostStatus(...)` maps `DockStreamFreshnessDTO(status: .stale)` to `.partial(rowCount: message:)`.
55	  - Existing test `DockStoreStreamTests.test...` asserts stale heartbeat retains rows and reports partial.
56	- The connectivity layer treats `.partial` as online-like.
57	  - `HostConnectivityPhase.isOnlineLike` returns true for `.online` and `.partial`.
58	  - `GlobalConnectivityIndicatorView` displays partial multi-host states as `Online N/N`, not `Partial` or `Stale`.
59	- Result: the simulator can truthfully show `Online 2/2` while the Dock list is sourced from stale retained rows.
60	
61	### 2026-05-31T17:09:01Z - Phone config check
62	
63	- Ran `rtk make device-config-verify-all`.
64	- iPhone 17 Pro device config verifies hosts:
65	  - `amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`
66	  - `home.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`
67	- iPhone 14 device config verifies hosts:
68	  - `Amir-M5.local:4510`
69	  - `192.168.50.74:4510`
70	- This confirms the phone app path points at the same relay-backed architecture. I did not reinstall or modify the phone app.
71	
72	### 2026-05-31T17:09Z - Final report saved
73	
74	- Saved final report:
75	  - `docs/CODEX_DOCK_STALENESS_ARCHITECTURE_ROOT_CAUSE_REPORT_2026-05-31.md`
76	- Main finding:
77	  - Stale Dock freshness is intentionally retained by the relay, converted to `partial` by the Swift Dock store, counted as online-like by connectivity, and displayed as `Online N/N` by the global badge.
78	- No implementation fix was made.
79	
80	### 2026-05-31T17:38Z - Missing-current-work clarification
81	
82	- Rechecked the active Amir thread `019e7e7d-66ca-7280-9aa0-2e272f1752b1`.
83	- `thread/read` still reports `updatedAt=1780238608` (`2026-05-31T14:43:28Z`).
84	- `thread/turns/list` reports newer turns, including:
85	  - `startedAt=1780249079` (`2026-05-31T17:37:59Z`)
86	  - `startedAt=1780246962` (`2026-05-31T17:02:42Z`)
87	- Clarification added to the final report:
88	  - Current turn data exists, but the Dock card source is built from thread-level projection fields, and those fields are not reflecting the latest turn activity.
